title: A quantitative inequality for general area-minimizing hypercones
summary: Let $\mathbf{C}=\partial E\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ be an area-minimizing hypercone. The cone may have nonisolated singularities. We prove that there is a constant $c_{\mathbf{C}}>0$ such that \[ \frac{\operatorname{Per}(F;B_R)-\operatorname{Per}(E;B_R)}{R^n} \geq c_{\mathbf{C}} \left(\frac{|F\triangle E|}{R^{n+1}}\right)^2 \] for every $R>0$ and every set $F$ of locally finite perimeter with $F\triangle E\Subset B_R$.
